mainTopic: The end of the story about רבי זירא's father, an honest tax collector, and then the גמרא's explanation of רבי שמעון's statement in the משנה about people who deal in שביעית produce.
overview: This amud opens at the end of a story about רבי זירא's father, an honest tax collector who protected his town and even returned money he did not need. The גמרא then explains רבי שמעון's remark in the משנה about people who deal in שביעית produce. רב יהודה's explanation is challenged by בני רחבה, so the גמרא reverses it: at first gatherers and merchants were both disqualified, but once heavy ארנונא taxes pressed people, gatherers became kosher witnesses while merchants stayed פסול. Next comes a story: ריש לקיש travels with two חכמים going to make a leap year. Along the way he complains about כהנים plowing and pruning in שביעית. The גמרא explains why he assumed they were כהנים, proving from a teaching about תרומה that כהנים were suspected about שביעית. ריש לקיש then tells רבי יוחנן that judges suspected about שביעית are a 'group of the wicked' that does not count, and רבי יוחנן agrees. Finally, the גמרא traces the idea of a wicked group that does not count to the story of שבנא, who betrayed חזקיה during סנחריב's siege and was punished measure for measure.

steps.title: Everyone hides when the official comes
steps.stepSummary: Everyone in town hides, and רבי זירא's father tells the official there is nobody to tax.
steps.simpleTranslation: And everyone would hide. When the official arrived, he would say to him: From whom should I collect?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues a story it started earlier. רבי זירא's father had the townspeople hide, so that when the tax official came, he could say the town was nearly empty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the town looked empty, the official could only demand a small tax. Even while working as a tax collector, the father was quietly protecting the people.

phrases.english: And everyone would hide.
When he would come, he would say to him:
phrases.notes: The one who comes is the higher tax official. The one speaking is רבי זירא's father.

phrases.english: From whom shall I request [taxes]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a story that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זירא's father used his job as tax collector to shield the townspeople from heavy taxes.

steps.title: He returns money on his deathbed
steps.stepSummary: Before he dies, the father tells his family to give back thirteen coins he took from someone and never needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he was dying, he said to them: Take thirteen coins tied up in my sheet and give them back to so-and-so. I took them from him, but I did not end up needing them.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the father returning money he had collected but did not have to pass on as tax.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This last scene shows how honest he was. He would not keep even a few coins that were not truly owed. The story shows that a tax collector is not always a dishonest person.

keyTerms.meaning: When he was dying (literally, when his soul was at rest)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's father was a tax collector who protected his town and even returned money he did not need. He was an honest man in a job that usually made people suspect.

phrases.english: When he was dying, he said to them:
Take thirteen ma'a coins
that are tied up for me in my sheet,
and return them to so-and-so,
for I took them from him
and I did not need them.
phrases.notes: He means he never had to pass these coins on as tax, so they still belonged to that person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story about רבי זירא's father.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An honest tax collector exists. רבי זירא's father returned even money he did not strictly need to return.

steps.title: Quoting רבי שמעון from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes רבי שמעון: at first people were called 'gatherers of שביעית produce.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: At first they would call them 'gatherers of שביעית produce.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the story and goes back to quote a line from the משנה. This sets up a question about what רבי שמעון meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed סוחרי שביעית, people who trade in שביעית produce, as unfit witnesses. רבי שמעון adds that at first a different name was used, אוספי שביעית. His point is unclear, so the גמרא will ask about it next.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year, when fields rest and produce may not be traded for profit

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
Initially they would call them
'Gatherers of Sabbatical-year produce.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: בַּתְּחִילָּה הָיוּ קוֹרְאִין אוֹתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the story back to the text of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון says the term originally used was 'gatherers of שביעית produce.'

steps.title: What does רבי שמעון mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון is trying to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון meant. This is a real question that sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'they called them gatherers' do not clearly state a law. So the גמרא wants to know what legal point is hidden in this change of name.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? (a request to explain a statement)

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the quote in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What legal point is behind רבי שמעון's remark about the name 'gatherers of שביעית'?

steps.title: רב יהודה explains: gatherers are kosher, merchants are not
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that at first the rule was: gatherers of שביעית produce are kosher witnesses, but merchants are disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: This is what he means. At first they would say: gatherers of שביעית produce are kosher, and merchants are disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question. He explains that רבי שמעון is describing the original law about who may serve as a witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Originally there was a difference between two kinds of people. Someone who only gathered a lot of שביעית produce for himself was still a kosher witness. Only someone who did business with it was פסול. So רבי שמעון's remark is really about a rule, not just a name.

keyTerms.meaning: Kosher, fit to serve as witnesses

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two groups. 'Gatherers' (אוספי) only collect the produce, while 'merchants' (סוחרין) sell it. At first, only the merchants were disqualified.
steps.whatToRemember: At first, the rule was that gatherers of שביעית produce were kosher witnesses, and only merchants of שביעית produce were פסול.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: This is what he is saying:
Initially they would say:
Gatherers of Sabbatical-year produce are fit,
phrases.notes: He means fit to be witnesses, since the משנה is listing who is disqualified from testifying.

phrases.english: merchants are disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון means that originally gatherers of שביעית produce were kosher witnesses and only merchants of it were disqualified.

steps.title: Later, both gatherers and merchants became disqualified
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה finishes his explanation: once people began paying the poor to gather שביעית produce for them, gathering turned into a business, so both gatherers and merchants were disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once there were many people giving money to the poor, and the poor would go and gather the produce for them and bring it, the חכמים changed the rule and said: both gatherers and merchants are disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of רב יהודה's explanation from the last step. He tells us how the rule changed: later on, gatherers were disqualified too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first, gathering a little שביעית produce for yourself was harmless, so gatherers stayed kosher witnesses. But when rich people started hiring the poor to gather for them, gathering became a hidden business. So the gatherers were now treated like the merchants, and both were disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: People who hand out money (here: who pay the poor to gather for them)
They changed the rule and said

phrases.english: Once those who gave money to the poor grew many,
and the poor would go and gather for them and bring it,
they changed and said:
both this one and that one are disqualified.
phrases.notes: 'This one and that one' means the gatherers and the merchants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יהודה's answer begun in step 5, describing the later change in the rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי שמעון is teaching in the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First gatherers were kosher and merchants disqualified; later, when the poor were hired to gather, both were disqualified.

steps.title: The words of the משנה don't fit this explanation
steps.stepSummary: The בני רחבה object: if the change came from too much trading, the משנה should have said 'once the merchants grew many,' not 'once the אנסים grew many.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The sons of רחבה had a problem with this: why does the משנה say 'once the אנסים (forceful tax collectors) grew many'? According to רב יהודה it should have said 'once the merchants grew many'!
steps.whatsHappening: The בני רחבה challenge רב יהודה's explanation. They say it does not match the actual words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה made the change about business getting worse, which made the rule stricter. But the משנה links the change to the אנסים, harsh tax collectors. Tax pressure is a reason to be more lenient, not stricter, so the explanation and the wording don't fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: They had a difficulty with it
People who use force; here, harsh tax collectors

phrases.english: The sons of Rachava had a difficulty with it:
This phrase, 'once the oppressors grew many'?
It should have said 'once the merchants grew many'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יהודה's explanation from steps 5–6 based on the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's order of events (lenient first, then stricter because of hired gatherers).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה ties the change to אנסים (tax collectors), but רב יהודה's explanation ties it to growing trade; the wording should then have mentioned merchants.

steps.title: A new explanation: taxes made the rule more lenient
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reverses the order: at first both gatherers and merchants were disqualified, but once heavy ארנונא taxes pushed people to work their land in שביעית, gatherers were made kosher while merchants stayed disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, at first they said: both gatherers and merchants are disqualified. Once the אנסים grew many — who are they? The ארנונא tax collectors, as רבי ינאי announced: 'Go out and plant in שביעית because of the ארנונא.' Then they changed and said: gatherers are kosher, merchants are disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב יהודה's version and explains רבי שמעון in the opposite order. This new version fits the משנה's word אנסים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the change goes from strict to lenient. Heavy taxes forced people to deal with their fields even in שביעית, so gatherers were no longer seen as sinners and became kosher witnesses again. Merchants who trade in שביעית produce stayed disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (dropping the earlier explanation for a new one)
A heavy government tax on produce or land
Merchants who trade in שביעית produce

steps.whatToRemember: The final version: at first gatherers and merchants were both disqualified; after the heavy ארנונא tax, gatherers became kosher witnesses, but merchants stayed disqualified.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix the two versions. רב יהודה's version (steps 5–6) went from lenient to strict; the version the גמרא keeps goes from strict to lenient.

phrases.english: Rather, at first they would say:
both this one and that one are disqualified.
Once the oppressors grew many —
and what are they? The arnona tax —
as Rabbi Yannai announced:
'Go out and sow in the seventh year because of the arnona.'
they changed and said:
gatherers are fit, merchants are disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the בני רחבה's challenge by replacing רב יהודה's explanation with one that fits the word אנסים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the order of the change is reversed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The change was from lenient to strict because trading grew.
steps.terutzMaskana: The change was from strict to lenient because heavy ארנונא taxes forced people to work the land in שביעית; gatherers became kosher, merchants stayed disqualified.

steps.title: Two rabbis go to make a leap year, and ריש לקיש joins them
steps.stepSummary: A new story: רבי חייא בר זרנוקי and רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק travel to עסיא to make a leap year, and ריש לקיש joins them to see how it is done.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר זרנוקי and רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק were going to make a leap year in עסיא. ריש לקיש met them and joined them. He said: I will go and see how they do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story connected to the topic of שביעית. This step only sets the scene; the main point of the story comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two rabbis are traveling to עסיא, outside ארץ ישראל, to add a month to the year (making a leap year). ריש לקיש tags along because he wants to watch how this is actually done. The story is setting up what will happen on the trip.

keyTerms.meaning: To make the year a leap year by adding a month

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר זַרְנוֹקֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Zarnokei and Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak
were going to make a leap year in Asya.
Reish Lakish met them,
he joined them.
He said: I will go and see
how they do the deed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר זַרְנוֹקֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק הֲווֹ קָאָזְלִי לְעַבֵּר שָׁנָה בְּעַסְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rule about שביעית witnesses to a new story loosely connected to שביעית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setting the scene: two rabbis travel to עסיא to make a leap year, and ריש לקיש joins to watch how it is done.

steps.title: ריש לקיש sees a man plowing
steps.stepSummary: On the trip, ריש לקיש sees a man plowing in שביעית and cries out that a כהן is plowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He saw a certain man plowing. He said to them: A כהן, and he is plowing!
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: ריש לקיש spots someone plowing during שביעית and complains about it. This sets up the חכמים's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plowing in שביעית is forbidden, so ריש לקיש is shocked to see a כהן doing it. His cry is really a complaint against the man.

keyTerms.meaning: the seventh year, when farm work in ארץ ישראל is forbidden

phrases.english: He saw a certain man who was plowing.
phrases.notes: 'He' is ריש לקיש, who joined the trip to עסיא in the last step.

phrases.english: He said to them: A priest, and plowing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the trip to עסיא begun in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plowing man's conduct during שביעית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Plowing is forbidden in שביעית, so a כהן seen plowing appears to be breaking the law.

steps.title: He may be a hired worker
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים defend the man: he could say he is only a hired worker on the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: He can say, 'I am a hired worker in it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The other חכמים give the plowing man the benefit of the doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the field belongs to a non-Jew and the man is only working there for pay, his plowing may be allowed. So we cannot assume he is breaking שביעית.

phrases.english: They said to him: He could say:
"I am a hired worker in it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's complaint from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Offers an innocent explanation for the act
steps.terutzMaskana: He may be a hired worker on a non-Jew's field.

steps.title: ריש לקיש sees a man pruning vines
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש sees a second man pruning vineyards and again cries out that a כהן is doing forbidden work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Again he saw a certain man cutting in the vineyards. He said to them: A כהן, and he is pruning!
steps.whatsHappening: A second story with the same pattern: ריש לקיש complains about someone pruning vines in שביעית. This sets up another defense from the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pruning (זמירה) is also forbidden farm work in שביעית. ריש לקיש again assumes the worst.

phrases.english: Again he saw a certain man
who was cutting in the vineyards.
He said to them: A priest, and pruning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, parallel story to step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The pruning man's conduct during שביעית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pruning vines is forbidden in שביעית, so a כהן seen pruning appears to be breaking the law.

steps.title: He may need the branches for a press basket
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים defend the man: he could say he needs the cut branches to make a basket for his olive press.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: He can say, 'I need it for a basket for the olive press.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים again give the man the benefit of the doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he is cutting the branches only because he needs the wood, and not to help the vines grow, the cutting may be allowed in שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: a woven basket used to hold olives in the press

phrases.english: They said to him: He could say:
"I need it for a basket for the olive press."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's complaint from step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Offers an innocent purpose for the act
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He is pruning to help the vines.
steps.terutzMaskana: He may only want the branches to make a press basket.

steps.title: The heart knows the real reason
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rejects the excuse with a wordplay: the heart knows if it is for an עקל or for crookedness.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The heart knows whether it is for a press basket or for crookedness.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש pushes back on the חכמים's defense of the pruning man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He suggests the 'basket' excuse is only a cover story. Only the man himself knows if he really needs the branches or is secretly pruning his vines.

phrases.english: He said to them: The heart knows
whether it is for a basket or for crookedness.
phrases.notes: A play on words: עקל (basket) sounds like עקלקלות (crookedness).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense given in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The excuse of needing branches for a basket.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is easy to claim and may just hide forbidden pruning.

steps.title: Which story came first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the two complaints ריש לקיש made first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which did he say to them first?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the order of the two stories. This sets up the reasoning in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order matters, because the excuse used in one story could have been used in the other.

phrases.english: Which did he say to them first?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the stories to ask about their order.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the two incidents happened first.

steps.title: The plowing story cannot be first
steps.stepSummary: If the plowing story came first, the חכמים would have used the 'hired worker' excuse again for the pruner.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he said the first one (plowing) first, then here too they should have said, 'I am a hired worker in it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one option, that the plowing story came first, and rules it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Hired worker' is a stronger excuse than 'I need branches.' If the חכמים had already thought of it, they would have used it for the pruner too. Since they did not, the plowing story was not first.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (introduces an option to test)

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵימָא הָא קַמַּיְיתָא אֲמַר לְהוּ בְּרֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: If you say he told them the first one first,
phrases.notes: 'The first one' is the plowing story, the one written first.

phrases.english: then for this one too, let them say: "I am a hired worker in it"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא הָא קַמַּיְיתָא אֲמַר לְהוּ בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one possible answer to the question in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the plowing story came first.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חכמים would then have reused the stronger 'hired worker' excuse.

steps.title: The pruning story came first
steps.stepSummary: So the pruning story came first, and only afterward the plowing story.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he said this one (pruning) first, and then he said that one (plowing).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the pruning complaint came first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the time of the pruning story, the חכמים had not yet thought of the 'hired worker' excuse. They came up with it later, in the plowing story.
steps.whatToRemember: Pruning came first, then plowing. Otherwise the חכמים would have reused the 'hired worker' excuse.

phrases.english: Rather, he told them this one first,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the pruning story.

phrases.english: and then he told them that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the other option in step 16, gives the answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The pruning story came first, the plowing story second.

steps.title: Why call him a כהן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ריש לקיש assumed the worker was a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a כהן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why ריש לקיש said 'a כהן' each time. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man's being a כהן seems unrelated to the work, so the גמרא wants to know why ריש לקיש brought it up.

phrases.english: What is different about a priest?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a detail in both stories.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why ריש לקיש assumed the man was a כהן.

steps.title: כהנים were suspected about שביעית
steps.stepSummary: Because כהנים were suspected of not keeping שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they are suspected regarding שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that ריש לקיש singled out כהנים because they had a reputation for being lax about שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since כהנים were known to be suspected about שביעית, ריש לקיש guessed that this worker was one of them.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש assumed the workers were כהנים because כהנים were suspected of not keeping שביעית.

phrases.english: Because they are suspected about the Sabbatical Year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כהנים were suspected of not keeping שביעית.

steps.title: A teaching about תרומה mixed into שביעית produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a teaching as the source for the claim that כהנים were suspected about שביעית: one סאה of תרומה that falls into a hundred סאה of שביעית produce is cancelled out, but if there is less, the mixture must rot.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: one סאה of תרומה that fell into a hundred סאה of שביעית produce is cancelled out. If there is less than that, the mixture must be left to rot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing proof for what it just said, that כהנים were suspected about שביעית. This teaching sets up the proof; the actual point comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה is only cancelled out when the other produce is at least a hundred times larger. If the mixture is smaller, non-כהנים may not eat it, so the ruling says it must rot. The next step asks why it can't simply be given to a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: A unit of volume for measuring produce
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which only כהנים may eat
Literally 'it goes up'; it is cancelled out in the mixture
They must be left to rot

phrases.english: As we learned:
A se'a of terumah that fell
into a hundred se'a of Sabbatical-year produce is cancelled out.
Less than this, they must rot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for step 19's claim that כהנים were suspected about שביעית.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that כהנים were suspected of not keeping שביעית.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching that a mixture of תרומה in less than a hundred parts of שביעית produce must rot.

steps.title: Why not sell the mixture to a כהן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the mixture must rot. The owner could sell it to a כהן at the cheaper price of תרומה and leave out the value of the one סאה, which belongs to the כהן anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: We discussed this teaching: why must it rot? Let the owner sell it to a כהן at the price of תרומה, leaving out the value of that one סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling that the mixture must rot, because there seems to be an easy way to keep it from going to waste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן is allowed to eat תרומה, so selling him the whole mixture seems to fix the problem. The owner would charge the lower price of תרומה, since only כהנים can buy it, and would not charge for the one סאה that already belongs to a כהן. So why does the teaching waste the food?

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (the גמרא raises a question on a source)
At the price of תרומה (cheaper, since only כהנים can buy it)

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
Why must they rot?
Let him sell it to a kohen at the price of terumah,
except for the value of that se'a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling quoted in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the mixture with less than a hundred parts must rot.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Food should not be wasted when it could be sold to a כהן, who is allowed to eat תרומה.

steps.title: This shows כהנים were suspected about שביעית
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא in the name of עולא answers that the teaching does not let the mixture be sold to a כהן. This shows that כהנים were suspected of not keeping the rules of שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא said in the name of עולא: this tells us that כהנים were suspected about שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered, and this answer finishes the proof for step 19: we can't give the mixture to a כהן because כהנים were suspected about שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mixture is also שביעית produce, which has its own rules, such as not keeping it past the set time. If כהנים could be trusted with those rules, the teaching would let the mixture be sold to them. Since it says the mixture must rot, כהנים must have been suspected, and that is why ריש לקיש assumed the worker was a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: This tells us (a conclusion drawn from a source)

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling that the mixture must rot instead of being sold to a כהן proves that כהנים were suspected about שביעית. That explains why ריש לקיש thought the worker was a כהן.

phrases.english: And Rav Chiya said in the name of Ulla:
This tells us,
priests were suspected regarding the Sabbatical year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21 and completes the proof begun in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the ruling by drawing a conclusion from it: כהנים cannot be trusted with שביעית produce
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mixture could simply be sold to a כהן instead of being left to rot.
steps.terutzMaskana: It may not be sold to a כהן, because כהנים were suspected of not keeping the rules of שביעית produce.

steps.title: The חכמים escape ריש לקיש by climbing onto a roof
steps.stepSummary: The story continues. The two חכמים said ריש לקיש was a nuisance, and when they arrived they climbed onto a roof and pulled the ladder away so he couldn't follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: this one is a nuisance. When they arrived there, they went up to the roof and pulled the ladder out from under it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story. The two חכמים, tired of ריש לקיש's complaints, find a way to keep him from joining them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each time ריש לקיש complained, he was challenging his companions along the way. They decided he was too bothersome. Once they reached their destination, they went up to the roof and removed the ladder so he would be left below.

phrases.english: They said: This one is a nuisance.
phrases.notes: 'They' are the two חכמים traveling with ריש לקיש, and 'this one' is ריש לקיש himself.

phrases.english: When they arrived there,
they went up to the roof,
and pulled the ladder out from beneath it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about כהנים and שביעית, the גמרא returns to the story of the journey.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים found ריש לקיש a nuisance and kept him out by removing the ladder to the roof.

steps.title: ריש לקיש questions whether suspected people may add a month to the year
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש comes to רבי יוחנן and asks whether people suspected about שביעית are fit to add a month to the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש came before רבי יוחנן and said to him: Are people who are suspected about the laws of שביעית fit to add a month to the year?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש brings his complaint about the two חכמים to רבי יוחנן. He asks whether people who seem lax about שביעית can be judges for עיבור שנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש saw how the two חכמים acted, and he connects it to the earlier discussion about people suspected regarding שביעית. It is worded as a question, but it is really a challenge: if these judges are not fit, the month they added may not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Adding an extra month to the year, done by a special בית דין
People who are suspected (of not keeping a law)
The seventh year, when the land must rest

phrases.english: He came before Rabbi Yochanan.
phrases.notes: "He" is ריש לקיש, who had been following the two חכמים.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּנֵי אָדָם הַחֲשׁוּדִין עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית,
phrases.english: He said to him: People who are suspected about the Seventh Year,
are they fit to add a month to the year?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנֵי אָדָם הַחֲשׁוּדִין עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית, כְּשֵׁרִין לְעַבֵּר שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the two חכמים escaped him, ריש לקיש raises his objection with רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The validity of the year-extension done by the two חכמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Judges suspected about שביעית may be unfit, so the month they added may not count.

steps.title: ריש לקיש suggests the case is like the three cattle herders
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers his own question: just as with the three cattle herders, the חכמים relied on their own calculation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he said: This is not hard for me. It is just like the case of the three cattle herders, where the חכמים relied on their own calculation.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש tries to answer his own question. He compares this case to an earlier story where the year was extended in line with what three cattle herders said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the cattle herders' story, the herders were not real judges, but that was fine because the חכמים relied on their own calculation. ריש לקיש suggests that here too, perhaps the real decision came from proper calculation, so the judges' status would not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like (a comparison to another case)

phrases.english: Then he said: It is not difficult for me,
it is just like the case of three cattle herders,
phrases.notes: This points back to an earlier story (סנהדרין 18b), where a month was added based on what three cattle herders said.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis relied on their own calculation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: ריש לקיש offers a possible answer to his own challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to an earlier case (the three cattle herders)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Judges suspected about שביעית would make the year-extension invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps it is valid, because the real basis was the חכמים' own calculation, as in the cattle herders' case.

steps.title: ריש לקיש rejects the comparison: a group of wicked people does not count
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש takes back the comparison. With the herders, the real חכמים voted afterward; here the judges themselves are wicked, and such a group does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he said: It is not similar. There, the חכמים voted afterward and added a month to that year. Here, it is a group of wicked people, and a group of wicked people does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש changes his mind and shows why the cattle herders' case is different. His original challenge comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the herders' case, the herders only gave information, and proper חכמים made the actual decision. Here the judges themselves are the problem, so there is no proper court behind the decision. A group of wicked people is not counted as a court.

keyTerms.meaning: Part of the count, counting toward the needed number

phrases.english: And then he said: It is not similar.
There, the Rabbis afterward voted
and added a month to that year.
Here, it is a group of wicked people,
and a group of wicked people does not count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison offered in step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison to the three cattle herders
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the herders' case, proper חכמים made the decision. Here the deciding judges are themselves unfit.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן admits the problem is serious
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says: This is troubling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This is a real problem.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן responds to ריש לקיש and agrees that his objection is troubling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not push back against ריש לקיש. By calling it a problem, he accepts that the judges' behavior raises a real concern.

keyTerms.meaning: This is troubling, this is a real difficulty

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: This is troubling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן reacts to ריש לקיש's final argument and accepts it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן agrees that ריש לקיש's objection is a real problem.

steps.title: The two חכמים complain to רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The two חכמים come to רבי יוחנן and complain that ריש לקיש called them 'cattle herders' and he said nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they came before רבי יוחנן, they said to him: He called us 'cattle herders,' and you did not say anything at all to him?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the two חכמים who added the month come to רבי יוחנן. They are upset that he did not defend them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש had compared them to the cattle herders, people not fit to be judges. They challenge רבי יוחנן for staying silent, as if he should have protected their honor.

keyTerms.meaning: Master, a respectful way to say 'you'

phrases.english: When they came before Rabbi Yochanan,
phrases.notes: "They" are the two חכמים who added the month, רבי חייא בר זרנוקי and רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק.

phrases.english: they said to him: He called us "cattle herders,"

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר וְלָא מִידֵּי?
phrases.english: and the Master did not say anything at all to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרֵי לַן רוֹעֵי בָקָר, וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר וְלָא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The story moves on. The two חכמים respond to how ריש לקיש described them.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's silence when ריש לקיש insulted them
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Calling חכמים 'cattle herders' is insulting, so רבי יוחנן should have objected.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even a harsher label would have been hard to answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that even if ריש לקיש had called them 'shepherds,' he could not have argued with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: And if he had called you 'shepherds,' what could I have said to him?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the two חכמים' complaint. He tells them he would have had no answer even for a harsher insult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shepherds of sheep and goats are viewed as worse than cattle herders. By saying he could not even have argued against that, רבי יוחנן shows that he agrees with ריש לקיש's criticism of their conduct.

keyTerms.meaning: What could I say to him?

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש argued that people suspected about שביעית are a 'group of wicked people' who do not count for עיבור שנה. רבי יוחנן agreed, and he did not defend the two חכמים even when they complained.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: וְאִי קָרֵי לְכוּ ״רוֹעֵי צֹאן״,
phrases.english: He said to them: And if he had called you "shepherds,"
what could I have said to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי קָרֵי לְכוּ רוֹעֵי צֹאן, מַאי אָמֵינָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the complaint raised in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the complaint and affirms the criticism
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן should have defended the two חכמים against the insult.
steps.terutzMaskana: The criticism was justified. Even a harsher label would have been hard to refute.

steps.title: Where does the idea of a 'conspiracy of the wicked' come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the phrase and rule of קשר רשעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this 'conspiracy of wicked people'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the idea of a 'wicked conspiracy that doesn't count' comes from. This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 26, ריש לקיש said a group of wicked judges does not count as a real group. The גמרא now wants to know where that idea and its wording come from. The answer will be a story from the time of King חזקיה.

keyTerms.meaning: A conspiracy or plot; a group banded together

phrases.english: What is 'a conspiracy of wicked people'?
phrases.notes: This phrase points back to what ריש לקיש said in step 26, that such a group does not count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the term ריש לקיש used in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The origin of the concept that a conspiracy of the wicked is not counted.

steps.title: שבנא's larger following and his secret surrender note
steps.stepSummary: שבנא had more followers than חזקיה. During סנחריב's siege, he shot a note over the wall saying that he and his group had surrendered.
steps.simpleTranslation: שבנא taught 130,000 people, while חזקיה taught only 110,000. When סנחריב came and surrounded ירושלים, שבנא wrote a note and shot it out on an arrow: 'שבנא and his group have made peace; חזקיה and his group have not.' As the פסוק says: 'For behold, the wicked bend the bow, they have set their arrow on the string.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer with a story. It sets up the problem: the wicked שבנא had the bigger group, and that group surrendered to the enemy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The numbers are important: שבנא's camp of 130,000 was larger than חזקיה's camp of 110,000. So by a simple count, the majority had sided with the enemy. The פסוק about the wicked shooting arrows is read as a hint to שבנא's arrow-note.

keyTerms.meaning: A minister in King חזקיה's court
They made peace, meaning they surrendered

phrases.english: Shebna would teach to thirteen ten-thousands,

phrases.aramaic: חִזְקִיָּה הֲוָה דָּרֵישׁ בְּחַד סַר רִבְּוָותָא.
phrases.english: Hezekiah would teach to eleven ten-thousands.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא סַנְחֵרִיב וְצַר עֲלַהּ דִּירוּשְׁלֶם,
phrases.english: When Sennacherib came and besieged Jerusalem,
Shebna wrote a note and shot it with an arrow:
"Shebna and his group have made peace,
Hezekiah and his group have not made peace."
As it is stated: "For behold, the wicked bend the bow,
phrases.notes: תהלים 11:2

phrases.english: they have set their arrow on the string."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to step 30 by telling the background story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Background: the wicked שבנא led a majority that secretly surrendered to סנחריב.

steps.title: The נביא tells חזקיה that a wicked majority does not count
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה feared that God would follow the majority. The נביא answered him with a פסוק: a conspiracy of the wicked is not counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה was afraid. He said: 'Maybe, God forbid, הקדוש ברוך הוא will follow the majority. Since the majority have been handed over to the enemy, the rest will be handed over too.' A נביא came and told him: 'Do not call it a conspiracy, all that this people calls a conspiracy.' This means: it is a conspiracy of wicked people, and a conspiracy of wicked people is not counted.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual source for the rule. The פסוק teaches that a wicked group does not count toward a majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the majority decides, so חזקיה feared that the bigger, surrendering camp would decide everyone's fate. The נביא used the word קשר, meaning 'conspiracy', to show that a wicked group is not part of the count at all. This is exactly the idea ריש לקיש used in step 26 about wicked judges.

keyTerms.meaning: Are handed over, here to the enemy
Is not part of the count

steps.whatToRemember: A 'conspiracy of the wicked' (קשר רשעים) is not counted, even if it is larger. That is why the wicked judges in step 26 do not count as a group.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the majority rule is cancelled in general. It is an exception: a group that bands together for wickedness is simply not counted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for ריש לקיש's rule in step 26, which explains why a court of wicked judges cannot act like a real group.

phrases.english: Hezekiah was afraid; he said:
Perhaps, God forbid,

phrases.aramaic: נָטְיָה דַּעְתֵּיהּ דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא בָּתַר רוּבָּא,
phrases.english: the mind of the Holy One, Blessed be He, will lean toward the majority,
and since the majority are handed over,
they too will be handed over.
A prophet came and said to him:
"Do not call it a conspiracy,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 8:12

phrases.aramaic: לְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יֹאמַר הָעָם הַזֶּה קָשֶׁר״,
phrases.english: all that this people calls a conspiracy,"
meaning: it is a conspiracy of wicked people,
and a conspiracy of wicked people is not counted.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא נָבִיא וְאָמַר לוֹ: לֹא תֹאמְרוּן קֶשֶׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story and gives the פסוק that answers step 30.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a conspiracy of the wicked is not counted (step 26).
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 8:12, read as: a wicked conspiracy is not part of the count.

steps.title: שבנא carves a grave among the royal tombs and is rebuked
steps.stepSummary: שבנא went to carve himself a grave among the graves of בית דוד, and the נביא scolded him and warned that God would cast him away.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went to carve out a grave for himself among the graves of בית דוד. A נביא came and told him: 'What do you have here, and who do you have here, that you carved yourself a grave here?... Behold, God will toss you about like a man is tossed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues about שבנא. He tried to place himself among the kings of בית דוד, and the נביא rebuked him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carving a grave in the royal tombs shows that שבנא was acting as if he belonged with the kings. The נביא asks what right he has to be there. He warns that God will throw him away instead, so the wicked group's leader will not succeed.

keyTerms.meaning: The burial place of the kings of David's family
Will toss you about or cast you away

phrases.english: He went to carve out a grave for himself
phrases.notes: 'He' is שבנא, not חזקיה.

phrases.english: among the graves of the house of David.
A prophet came and said to him:
"What do you have here, and whom do you have here,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 22:16

phrases.english: that you have carved yourself a grave here?...
Behold, the Lord will toss you about like the tossing of a man."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 22:17

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלַךְ לַחְצֹב לוֹ קֶבֶר בְּקִבְרֵי בֵּית דָּוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the שבנא story after the main point has been proven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבנא tried to place himself among the kings, and the נביא foretold that God would cast him away.

steps.title: A man's wandering is harder than a woman's
steps.stepSummary: רב makes a side remark: when a man is forced to wander from place to place, it is harder for him than for a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The wandering of a man is harder than the wandering of a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses for a quick side comment from רב on a phrase in the prophecy against שבנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נביא threatened שבנא with 'the wandering of a man' (ישעיהו 22:17). רב reads the word 'man' as a hint that being uprooted is especially hard for a man. This is a side point; right after it the גמרא goes back to explaining the prophecy.

keyTerms.meaning: Wandering, being uprooted and moved from place to place

phrases.english: Rav said:
The wandering of a man
phrases.notes: This is built on the פסוק's words about שבנא, 'like the wandering of a man' (ישעיהו 22:17).

phrases.english: is harder than that of a woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: טִלְטוּלָא דְּגַבְרָא קָשֵׁי מִדְּאִיתְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side comment on a word from the prophecy against שבנא that began in step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being forced to wander is harder for a man than for a woman.

steps.title: שבנא was struck with צרעת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains that the words 'he will wrap you' mean שבנא was struck with צרעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the words 'and he will wrap you up,' רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: This teaches that צרעת broke out on שבנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the prophecy and explains one more phrase: שבנא was punished with צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, 'wrapping' sounds like a picture of being thrown away. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says it points to a real punishment, צרעת. His proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And he will wrap you up (a phrase from the prophecy)
A skin disease from the Torah, often called leprosy

phrases.english: "And he will wrap you up":
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 22:17

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, said:
This teaches that leprosy broke out on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעֹטְךָ עָטֹה – אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁפָּרְחָה בּוֹ צָרַעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רב's side remark and goes back to explaining the prophecy against שבנא.

steps.title: Proof from a matching word in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The same word, 'wrap/cover,' appears in the Torah about a מצורע, so the prophecy is talking about צרעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says here 'and he will wrap you up,' and it says there, about a מצורע, 'and he shall cover his upper lip.'
steps.whatsHappening: Here רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא proves his claim that שבנא got צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word for 'wrap' in ישעיהו shares a root with the word for 'cover' in the Torah's laws of a מצורע, who must cover his upper lip. Because the same word appears in both places, the prophecy is read as talking about צרעת.

keyTerms.meaning: The upper lip or mustache area

phrases.english: It is written here: "And he will wrap you up,"
and it is written there
"and he shall cover his upper lip."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:45, said about a מצורע. Same root as 'wrap' in ישעיהו.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב הָכָא ״וְעֹטְךָ עָטֹה״, וּכְתִיב הָתָם ״וְעַל שָׂפָם יַעְטֶה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the proof for the claim in step 35.
steps.raayaObject: That שבנא was struck with צרעת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared word עטה in ישעיהו 22:17 and in ויקרא 13:45 about a מצורע

steps.title: He wanted shame for others, so he got shame himself
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the next פסוק: שבנא tried to shame his master's house, so his own honor was turned into shame.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He will wind you round tightly, like a ball into a wide land, etc.' A ברייתא taught: He wanted to bring shame on his master's house, so his honor was turned into shame.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק of the prophecy and quotes a ברייתא explaining why שבנא was punished this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבנא wanted to disgrace חזקיה's house by surrendering behind its back. The ברייתא says the punishment matched the crime: the shame he planned for others fell on him. The next step shows how this actually happened.

keyTerms.meaning: He will wind you round tightly

phrases.english: "He will wind you round tightly,

phrases.aramaic: כַּדּוּר אֶל אֶרֶץ רַחֲבַת יָדָיִם וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: like a ball into a wide land, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 22:18. The 'etc.' points to the end of the פסוק, which calls him 'the shame of your master's house.'

phrases.english: A baraita taught:
He sought the shame of his master's house,
therefore his honor was turned into shame.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הוּא בִּיקֵּשׁ קְלוֹן בֵּית אֲדֹנָיו, לְפִיכָךְ נֶהְפַּךְ כְּבוֹדוֹ לְקָלוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from ישעיהו 22:17 to the next פסוק, 22:18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because שבנא sought shame for his master's house, his own honor turned into shame.

steps.title: גבריאל shuts the gate on שבנא's followers
steps.stepSummary: As שבנא went out to surrender, the angel גבריאל shut the gate in front of his followers, so he went out alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: When שבנא was going out, גבריאל came and shut the gate in the face of his camp.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the story of how שבנא's honor turned into shame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבנא's whole plan depended on bringing a large group with him to surrender. Because גבריאל shut the gate, his followers were stuck inside and he came out alone. His big show of strength became an embarrassment.

keyTerms.meaning: His camp, his group of followers

steps.whatToRemember: שבנא was punished measure for measure: he got צרעת, and the shame he planned for חזקיה's house came back on him when he was left to surrender alone.

phrases.english: When he was going out,
Gabriel came
and shut the gate
in the face of his camp.
phrases.notes: So his followers couldn't get out after him, and he went out alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוָה נָפֵיק אִיהוּ, אֲתָא גַּבְרִיאֵל אַחְדֵּיהּ לְדַשָּׁא בְּאַפֵּי מַשְׁרְיָיתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells the story that shows how the ברייתא's rule in step 37 came true.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גבריאל shut the gate so that שבנא's followers could not leave with him.
